subtype: Approach: building a minimum viable version in six weeks [Action]
passage: Six weeks. That's what we gave ourselves. Himani and I sat in a borrowed room in Lucknow and built the ugliest invoicing tool you have ever seen, out of no-code tools and a spreadsheet. No custom backend, no login screen, nothing you would show in a pitch. I'm Gopika, by the way. At the end of week six we walked into twenty kirana shops with a phone, sat next to the shop owners and asked them to try it. Three said it was useless. Seven said they would pay if it printed in Hindi. One old shopkeeper pointed out that a button I would never have noticed was the wrong colour. We would have spent a year on the backend if we hadn't asked. Instead we spent our time fixing what people actually said.

qa.q: How many shop owners did Gopika and Himani show the tool to?
qa.a: They showed it to twenty shop owners.

qa.q: What does "the ugliest invoicing tool you have ever seen" suggest about how Gopika felt about showing it?
qa.a: It suggests Gopika felt a little embarrassed but was willing to show unfinished work anyway.

qa.q: What alternative approach could have worked instead of building a backend first?
qa.a: They could have asked shop owners about their invoicing habits first, or run the process by hand, because that also gets feedback before large work.

qa.q: How might the shop owners have felt being asked to try it?
qa.a: They may have felt listened to, since their comments about Hindi printing and the button colour were used.

grounding: Two founders build a bare-bones invoicing tool in six weeks with no-code tools and put it in front of twenty shop owners in Lucknow first.
